On 16 June, António Guterres visited Haiti in solidarity with the Haitian people and to assess the country’s security, humanitarian and political challenges. During the visit, he met with people affected by violence and reviewed efforts by national authorities and the international community to restore stability. Highlighting the scale of the crisis, the Secretary-General called for stronger international engagement, including support for security, humanitarian assistance and the political transition. Stressing the urgency of action, he said, “Haiti is not asking for charity. Haiti is asking the world to keep its promises.”

In Cap-Haïtien, on Haiti's north coast, national authorities, electoral institutions and civil society organizations, with support from the United Nations Integrated Office in Haiti (BINUH), conducted voter awareness and training activities for young people and women preparing to vote for the first time. The initiative highlighted the importance of broad participation in building an inclusive, transparent and representative electoral process. In line with its mandate, BINUH reaffirmed its commitment to supporting national efforts to organize credible elections, advance the political process and contribute to the restoration of democratic institutions in Haiti.

On 15 June, Kaha Imnadze, SRSG and Head of the United Nations Regional Centre for Preventive Diplomacy for Central Asia (UNRCCA), participated in the Eighth Meeting of Special Representatives and Envoys of the European Union and Central Asian countries on Afghanistan in Almaty. Discussions focused on developments in Afghanistan and their implications for regional security and prosperity. In his remarks, Mr. Imnadze highlighted concerns related to border security, terrorism, drug trafficking and the rights of minorities, women and girls, while underscoring the importance of Afghanistan’s integration into regional economic development processes.

On 17 June, Mr. Imnadze also participated in a High-Level Roundtable of Executive Structures of Regional Organizations in Asia in Astana. Discussions focused on the role of regional organizations in promoting dialogue, trust and cooperation. He highlighted the importance of cooperation between the United Nations and regional organizations in support of preventive diplomacy, peace and security.

On 17 June, the UNVMC accompanied the graduation of 30 peace signatories from the Urabá-Darién region who completed a course on citizen participation, advocacy and social oversight in Mutatá, Antioquia. Delivered through the Political Training School of the University of Antioquia and the Agency for Reincorporation and Normalization (ARN), the programme strengthened participants’ capacities to engage in democratic processes, exercise civic leadership and contribute to peacebuilding and local development in their communities.
Later this week, the annual Ukraine Recovery Conference will take place in Gdańsk, Poland, seeking to advance international efforts in support of Ukraine’s recovery and reconstruction.

On 26 June, the Department of Political and Peacebuilding Affairs (DPPA) and the Secretariat of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) held their fourth Secretariat-to-Secretariat Dialogue in New York, co-chaired by Assistant Secretary-General for Middle East, Europe, the Americas, Asia and the Pacific Khaled Khiari and SCO Deputy Secretary-General Ahmad Saidmurodzoda.

Discussions focused on Central Asia, where both organizations have developed close cooperation, including through engagement with the United Nations Regional Centre for Preventive Diplomacy for Central Asia (UNRCCA) and the SCO’s Regional Anti-Terrorist Structure. Participants highlighted the region’s growing role in promoting dialogue, confidence-building and regional ownership of peace and security initiatives.

Afghanistan featured prominently in the discussions. Participants exchanged views on the security, political, humanitarian and socio-economic situation, including counter-narcotics efforts, regional connectivity, human rights and the need for continued international engagement. Both sides stressed the importance of a stable Afghanistan for regional security and prosperity and discussed ongoing efforts to support dialogue and cooperation.

The meeting also addressed counter-terrorism, violent extremism, drug trafficking and other transnational threats, as well as climate, peace and security, highlighting the impact of climate change, water scarcity and environmental degradation on stability and development across Central Asia and Afghanistan.

From 24 to 26 June 2026, DPPA supported youth peacebuilders from China, Japan, and the ROK to participate in the 2026 Jeju Forum’s inaugural SPEAK program . The SPEAK is an international youth program that brings together young people to share their perspectives and ideas on global challenges, providing a platform for youth to present, exchange, and develop their visions for sustainable peace and the future.

On the margins of the Organization of American States (OAS) Summit in Panama, Under-Secretary-General (USG) for Political and Peacebuilding Affairs Rosemary DiCarlo met with the Foreign Ministers of Haiti and the Dominican Republic to discuss regional developments and support for Haiti. During her visit, USG DiCarlo also represented the Secretary-General at events commemorating the 200th anniversary of the Amphictyonic Congress of Panama, reaffirming the United Nations commitment to dialogue, cooperation and the peaceful resolution of differences.

On 26 June, USG Rosemary DiCarlo briefed the Security Council on the rapidly deteriorating situation in Sudan, warning that intensified fighting around El Obeid could place hundreds of thousands of civilians at immediate risk and further destabilize the wider Kordofan region. She called on the parties to exercise restraint, engage in good faith towards a humanitarian truce and support efforts toward a permanent ceasefire and an inclusive, Sudanese-owned political process. The USG also highlighted Personal Envoy of the Secretary-General (PESG) Pekka Haavisto’s engagement with the conflict parties and regional actors to help de-escalate violence and advance prospects for peace. Ahead of the briefing, on 25 June, PESG Haavisto also briefed the media , warning that any further escalation around El Obeid would place hundreds of thousands of civilians at risk.

Briefing the Security Council on Syria’s political transition on 22 June, Deputy Special Envoy of the Secretary-General (DSESG) Claudio Cordone said that the country is in “a critical phase, with opportunity and fragility existing side-by-side.” He highlighted the need to establish the People’s Assembly, advance transitional justice and ensure the meaningful participation of women and all components of Syrian society. DSESG Cordone also reported continued engagement between the United Nations and the Syrian authorities, while expressing concern over delays in the transition, developments in Sweida and continued Israeli military activity in southern Syria.

The UN Special Committee on Decolonization held its two-week June session from 15 to 26 June at Headquarters in New York. Chaired by Ambassador Menissa Rambally of Saint Lucia, the meeting brought together representatives from UN Member States, along with voices from Territories and petitioners.

During the session, representatives from the Territories and petitioners shared firsthand updates and concerns, including discussions on Puerto Rico. The Committee also explored broader issues, such as the implementation of the Declaration on Decolonization and the dissemination of information on decolonization. By the end of the meeting, the Committee considered 22 draft resolutions, many of which are recommended to General Assembly through the Fourth Committee.

On 24 June, Hans Grundberg, Special Envoy of the Secretary-General (SESG) for Yemen, concluded a visit to London , where he met with Minister for the Middle East Hamish Falconer, National Security Adviser Jonathan Powell, UK Ambassador to Yemen, Abda Sharif, as well as other senior UK officials, members of the diplomatic community and experts. Discussions focused on prospects for advancing an inclusive, internationally supported, Yemeni-led political process under UN auspices as the only viable path to long-term stability.

The Young Peacebuilders Cross-Border Initiative opened in Fergana Valley on 22 June, bringing together more than 30 young people from Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan and Uzbekistan to promote dialogue, trust and cooperation across the region. Held under the framework of the Fergana Peace Process, the initiative builds on the Kyrgyzstan–Tajikistan border agreement, the trilateral agreement and declaration adopted by Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan and Uzbekistan in Khujand while giving young people from border communities a practical role in advancing peace. Opening the event, Special Representative of the Secretary-General and Head of the United Nations Regional Centre for Preventive Diplomacy for Central Asia (UNRCCA) Kaha Imnadze stressed that “young people should not be observers of the Fergana Peace Process; they should be part of shaping its practical content.”

On 23 June, the United Nations Office for West Africa and the Sahel (UNOWAS) and the United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC) convened a multi-stakeholder workshop in Dakar to address the growing challenge posed by emerging drugs in Senegal. Bringing together government officials, regional organizations, UN entities, civil society and youth representatives, participants examined the impact of new psychoactive substances on public health, social cohesion and regional security. Discussions emphasized prevention, community-based responses and stronger cooperation between youth and security actors to build more resilient communities.

On 24 June, the United Nations Verification Mission in Colombia (UNVMC) joined the Agency for Reincorporation and Normalization (ARN) in delivering 147 homes to peace signatories at the Territorial Area for Training and Reintegration (TATR) in San Juan de Arama. The initiative marks an important step in supporting sustainable reintegration by promoting stability and long-term community integration. Recipients reaffirmed their commitment to implementing the 2016 Peace Agreement and to strengthening peaceful coexistence and dialogue with neighboring communities.

This week at the Jeju Forum, young peacebuilders participating in DPPA’s Futuring Peace in Northeast Asia initiative explored the importance of inclusive and responsible digital governance in advancing the Youth, Peace and Security and Women, Peace and Security agendas. They highlighted how intergenerational and cross-regional engagement has strengthened networks for peace and collaboration, and discussed the role of young women as leaders and peacebuilders in digital spaces. In a video message , ASG Khiari underscored DPPA’s support for youth leadership, stressing that young people “are not only the future of peace. They are its present.”

The Joint Meeting of the Peacebuilding Commission and the Economic and Social Council, "From Risk to Resilience: Advancing Social Cohesion Through Job Creation in Peacebuilding Contexts," examined how decent work and economic opportunity can strengthen social cohesion in places affected by conflict. A Peace Circle, "Financing and Partnerships for Youth-led Peacebuilding," placed young peacebuilders at the centre of the conversation on the financing and support their work needs to grow.

On inclusion, "From Geneva to New York: Taking Stock of the CSO-UN Dialogue on Peacebuilding," attended by Under-Secretary-General Rosemary DiCarlo , brought civil society, the UN and Member States together to reflect on how far the Dialogue process has come and where it goes next.
The Security Council is expected to hold a meeting on the Middle East on 29 June. In July, the Democratic Republic of the Congo will assume the presidency of the Security Council.

Ambassador Leonor Zalabata Torres, Permanent Representative of Colombia and President of the Security Council for June, highlighted the role of special political missions in facilitating dialogue, supporting reconciliation and strengthening national peacebuilding efforts. She welcomed the publication as a contribution to institutional knowledge and ongoing discussions on the future of UN peace operations.

Ambassador José Alberto Briz Gutiérrez, Permanent Representative of Guatemala and Chair of the General Assembly's Fourth Committee, underscored the historical relationship between special political missions and the realization of self-determination. Drawing on Guatemala's own peace process, he emphasized the importance of national ownership, sustained political dialogue and international accompaniment.

As USG DiCarlo concluded, the history of special political missions demonstrates that “even in the most difficult of circumstances, dialogue can open doors, patience can build trust, and diplomacy can change the course of history.”

On 30 June, Department of Political and Peacebuilding Affairs (DPPA) launched United Nations Special Political Missions 1945–2025: An Overview , the first comprehensive public record of UN special political missions since 1948. Speaking at the event , Under-Secretary-General (USG) for Political and Peacebuilding Affairs Rosemary DiCarlo reflected on nearly eight decades of UN peacemaking, conflict prevention and political transitions, emphasizing that the history of special political missions demonstrates that “diplomacy works.” She highlighted the adaptability of special political missions in responding to evolving peace and security challenges and reaffirmed the importance of diplomacy, dialogue and partnerships.

On 29 June, Deputy Special Coordinator of the Secretary-General for the Middle East Peace Process Ramiz Alakbarov briefed the Security Council on the implementation of resolution 2334 (2016), warning that the situation across Gaza and the West Bank, including East Jerusalem, remains deeply concerning. He highlighted continued hostilities in Gaza, the deteriorating humanitarian situation, expanding Israeli control over territory, and escalating violence and settlement activity in the West Bank. Reaffirming the Secretary-General’s position, the Deputy Special Coordinator called for the full implementation of resolution 2803 and renewed international efforts toward a negotiated two-State solution. The following day, he led a field visit to East Jerusalem with more than 20 diplomats, meeting communities affected by demolitions, evictions, movement restrictions and the threat of forcible tran

On 29 June, Assistant Secretary-General (ASG) for Africa Martha Pobee briefed the Security Council on the growing regional implications of the war in Ukraine, warning that escalating attacks and increasing reports of airspace violations and drone sightings across neighboring countries have heightened the risk of wider spillover. She called on all concerned Member States to avoid actions that could further escalate the conflict and urged renewed dialogue and diplomacy. Welcoming the latest exchange of prisoners of war and civilians between the parties, ASG Pobee stressed that “diplomacy can result in tangible outcomes” and reiterated the UN’s call for an immediate, full and unconditional ceasefire.

On 2 July, ASG for Peacebuilding and Peace Support Elizabeth Spehar briefed the Security Council on recent developments between the United States and Iran, welcoming the decision by both sides to de-escalate and resume dialogue following recent military confrontations. She underscored the fragility of the current situation, condemned attacks on civilians and civilian infrastructure, and stressed the need to protect freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz. Urging all parties to exercise “maximum restraint,” ASG Spehar reaffirmed the United Nations support for diplomacy to prevent a return to conflict and advance a durable resolution.

On 26 June, DPPA and the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) held their fourth Secretariat-to-Secretariat Dialogue at UN Headquarters, co-chaired by ASG Middle East, Europe, the Americas, Asia and the Pacific Khaled Khiari and SCO Deputy Secretary-General Ahmad Saidmurodzoda. The meeting also addressed counter-terrorism, violent extremism, drug trafficking and other transnational threats, as well as climate, peace and security, highlighting the impact of climate change, water scarcity and environmental degradation on stability and development across Central Asia and Afghanistan. Both sides reaffirmed their commitment to expand practical cooperation on shared priorities, including women, peace and security, youth engagement, climate and regional stability.

On 29 June, the UNVMC and the Office of the Ombudsman of Colombia (Defensoría del Pueblo) visited rural properties in the municipalities of Chimichagua, Tamalameque and Pailitas, in Cesar Department, and met with peasant organizations to discuss progress, challenges and opportunities related to land access and the Comprehensive Rural Reform. The visit underscored the importance of sustained dialogue with rural communities to support the implementation of the Final Peace Agreement and advance inclusive, sustainable rural development.

On 1 July, the United Nations Support Mission in Libya (UNSMIL) convened a public livestream with members of the Economic Track of the Structured Dialogue, providing Libyans from across the country with an opportunity to discuss recommendations to address the country’s long-standing economic challenges. Participants highlighted proposals to strengthen public financial governance, diversify the economy, improve transparency and promote more balanced regional development. The discussion underscored the importance of inclusive public engagement, with participants noting that implementation will require political consensus, stronger institutions and improved access to reliable economic data.

Jean Arnault, Officer-in-Charge of the Office of the United Nations Special Coordinator for Lebanon (UNSCOL) , who assumed his duties at the beginning of July, held a series of meetings with senior political and security officials in Lebanon to discuss reinforcing stability, strengthening state institutions and advancing the implementation of Security Council resolution 1701 (2006). His meetings, including with the President, Speaker of Parliament, Prime Minister, Deputy Prime Minister, Ministers of Interior and Defense, and the Commander of the Lebanese Armed Forces, provided an opportunity to review cooperation between Lebanon and the United Nations. He also travelled to Israel this week, where he met with senior Israeli officials to discuss the current situation.

On 13 July, Assistant Secretary-General for the Middle East, Europe, the Americas, Asia and the Pacific Khaled Khiari briefed the Security Council on recent developments in Yemen, warning that rising regional tensions risk triggering a new cycle of escalation. He reiterated that there is “no alternative to an inclusive, Yemeni-owned political process” under UN auspices and called on all parties to engage constructively in dialogue and refrain from unilateral actions that could undermine peace efforts. He also urged the immediate, safe and unconditional release of 73 UN personnel and other detainees arbitrarily held by the Houthis.

On 14 July, Special Representative of the Secretary-General (SRSG) and Head of the United Nations Office for West Africa and the Sahel (UNOWAS) Leonardo Santos Simão briefed the Security Council on developments in West Africa and the Sahel, highlighting persistent insecurity, renewed momentum for regional dialogue and cooperation, and ongoing democratic developments. While warning that terrorist groups continue to expand their operations and humanitarian needs remain severe, he welcomed diplomatic engagement between ECOWAS and the Alliance of Sahel States, as well as progress by the Cameroon-Nigeria Mixed Commission. Stressing that “security responses alone will not be enough,” the SRSG called for greater investment in the social, economic and environmental foundations of peace.

From 11 to 16 July, the SRSG and Head of the United Nations Regional Office for Central Africa (UNOCA) , Mohamed El-Amine Souef, visited São Tomé and Príncipe as part of his introductory tour of the 11 countries in the region. The visit, which coincided with the country's 51st anniversary of independence, provided an opportunity to engage with national authorities and key stakeholders and reaffirm the longstanding partnership between the United Nations and São Tomé and Príncipe.

On 13 July, Jean Arnault, Officer-in-Charge of the Office of the United Nations Special Coordinator for Lebanon (UNSCOL) [and Personal Envoy of the Secretary-General on the Middle East conflict and its consequences], visited Iran as part of his regional engagement on Lebanon . During meetings with Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi, he discussed the implementation of Security Council resolution 1701 (2006), the challenges facing Lebanon, and the support that regional countries can provide to Lebanon’s aspirations for peace, sovereignty and territorial integrity.

On 14 July, Special Envoy of the Secretary-General (SESG) for Yemen Hans Grundberg visited Muscat , where he met with senior Omani officials and Houthi’s chief negotiator, Mohamed Abdul Salam. The discussions focused on the need for immediate de-escalation and preserving the relative calm achieved since the 2022 UN-brokered truce. SESG Grundberg also called on the parties to engage in UN-facilitated negotiations across the political, military/security and economic tracks to advance a comprehensive and sustainable resolution to the conflict.

Geneva, 22 July 2026 — Senior representatives from the United Nations (UN) and the Organization of Islamic Cooperation (OIC) convened today in Geneva for the 17th General Cooperation Meeting between the two organizations and their specialized bodies.

Held every two years, the meeting brings together high-level representatives from nearly 50 UN and OIC agencies, funds and programmes to strengthen cooperation across a broad range of shared priorities.

The meeting is co-chaired by Ahmad Kawesa Sengendo, Assistant Secretary-General (ASG) for Economic Affairs of the OIC, and Khaled Khiari, Assistant Secretary-General for the Middle East, Europe, Central Asia and the Americas, Asia and the Pacific in the United Nations Departments of Political and Peacebuilding Affairs (DPPA) and Peace Operations (DPO).

Opening the meeting, ASG Khiari underscored the importance of the strong partnership between the UN and the OIC , highlighting decades of collaboration in conflict prevention and diplomacy, countering violent extremism, promoting the rights of women, addressing climate change, strengthening food security, delivering humanitarian assistance and combating Islamophobia and all forms of intolerance.

The General Cooperation Meeting, taking place from 22 to 24 July at the United Nations Office at Geneva, provides a platform for the United Nations and the OIC to review progress, identify new areas of cooperation and strengthen their strategic partnership in support of international peace and security.

On 19 July, Special Envoy of the Secretary-General (SESG) for Yemen, Hans Grundberg, visited Riyadh, where he met with the President of the Presidential Leadership Council, Rashad Al-Alimi, Saudi Ambassador to Yemen Mohammed Al Jaber, and representatives of the five permanent members of the Security Council. The discussions focused on the need for immediate de-escalation, preserving the gains of the 2022 UN-brokered truce, and advancing an inclusive, Yemeni-led political process.

On 23 July, SESG for the Horn of Africa, Guang Cong, visited Juba to meet with senior South Sudanese officials, including Foreign Minister James Pitia Morgan, and other stakeholders on the Joint Political and Security Mechanism (JPSM) and other Abyei-related issues. Discussions focused on resuming the JPSM, advancing the demilitarization of the Abyei Area, and addressing differing views on Abyei’s participation in South Sudan’s December 2026 elections. SESG Cong welcomed the commitment of Sudan and South Sudan to restart the JPSM and urged the parties to resolve outstanding issues through dialogue and de-escalate public rhetoric.

This week, Jean Arnault, Officer-in-Charge of the Office of the United Nations Special Coordinator for Lebanon (UNSCOL) [and Personal Envoy of the Secretary-General on the Middle East conflict and its consequences], held a series of meetings with Lebanese political leaders, government officials and parliamentarians to discuss the country’s fragile security situation, the implementation of Security Council resolution 1701 (2006) and the Trilateral Framework agreed by the United States, Lebanon and Israel. He also met with Finance Minister Yassine Jaber to discuss Lebanon’s economic situation and prospects for financial reforms. During a meeting with a delegation representing 86 Members of Parliament, on 23 July, he received a petition addressed to the Secretary-General calling for the renewal of UNIFIL’s mandate and thanked the delegation for its continued support for the United Nations a

From 22 to 24 July, senior representatives of the United Nations and the Organization of Islamic Cooperation (OIC) gathered in Geneva for the 17th General Cooperation Meeting . Co-chaired by Assistant Secretary-General (ASG) for the Middle East, Europe, Central Asia and the Americas, Asia and the Pacific Khaled Khiari and OIC Assistant Secretary-General Ahmad Kawesa Sengendo, the meeting brought together nearly 50 UN and OIC entities to strengthen cooperation on shared priorities, including conflict prevention, diplomacy, humanitarian action, women’s rights, climate change and countering violent extremism. ASG Khiari underscored that cooperation between the UN and regional organizations is a “force multiplier” in addressing today’s global challenges.

On 21 July, SRSG and Head of the United Nations Regional Centre for Preventive Diplomacy for Central Asia (UNRCCA) , Kaha Imnadze, met with Turkmenistan’s Deputy Chairman of the Cabinet of Ministers and Minister of Foreign Affairs, Rashid Meredov, in Ashgabat. The discussions focused on priorities for continued cooperation between Turkmenistan and UNRCCA, regional developments, and upcoming high-level regional and international events to be hosted by Turkmenistan in 2026, including opportunities for UNRCCA’s engagement through its preventive diplomacy mandate.
The Security Council is expected to hold a briefing on Ukraine on 27 July, followed by an open debate on the Middle East on 28 July.

Geneva, 27 July 2026 — The United Nations (UN) and the League of Arab States (LAS) are convening their General Cooperation Meeting at the United Nations Office at Geneva from 27 to 29 July, bringing together senior representatives from around 40 UN and LAS agencies, funds and programmes to strengthen collaboration across a range of shared priorities.

The meeting is co-chaired by LAS Assistant Secretary-General (ASG) and Head of the International Political Affairs Sector, Ambassador Khaled Manzlawiy, and United Nations Assistant Secretary-General for the Middle East, Europe, the Americas, Asia and the Pacific, Khaled Khiari, of the Departments of Political and Peacebuilding Affairs (DPPA) and Peace Operations (DPO).

Opening the meeting, Assistant Secretary-General Khiari stressed the importance of partnership in addressing today's increasingly complex global challenges. He described cooperation and joint action between the United Nations and the League of Arab States as "force multipliers" that enable both organizations to achieve far greater impact together than either could alone, for the benefit of the people they serve.

Over the course of the three-day meeting, participants will review ongoing cooperation, exchange expertise and explore opportunities to further strengthen collaboration in support of peace, security and sustainable development across the Arab region and beyond.

From 25 to 27 July, Secretary-General António Guterres made his first official visit to Syria, accompanied by Under-Secretaries-General Rosemary DiCarlo and Jean-Pierre Lacroix and the Deputy Special Envoy of the Secretary-General for Syria, Claudio Cordone. During meetings with President Ahmad Al-Sharaa, senior government officials, civil society representatives, women's organizations and members of Syria's diverse communities, the Secretary-General welcomed progress in the transition while emphasizing the importance of inclusive participation, accountability, transitional justice and reconciliation. The delegation also visited Sednaya Prison to pay tribute to the victims of the former regime.

From 28 to 29 July, the Secretary-General visited Cyprus as part of his good offices mission, accompanied by Under-Secretaries-General Rosemary DiCarlo and Jean-Pierre Lacroix and the Personal Envoy of the Secretary-General on Cyprus, María Ángela Holguín. He met separately and jointly with Greek Cypriot leader Nikos Christodoulides and Turkish Cypriot leader Tufan Erhürman, reaffirming the United Nations' commitment to supporting the Cypriots in their search for a comprehensive and sustainable settlement of the Cyprus issue.

On 29 July, the Security Council held consultations on the United Nations Regional Centre for Preventive Diplomacy for Central Asia (UNRCCA) where the Special Representative of the Secretary-General (SRSG) and Head of the UNRCCA, Kaha Imnadze, briefed Council members on the work of that office. Ahead of the briefing, on 23–24 July, the SRSG visited Washington, D.C . where he met with senior officials of the Department of State, the World Bank Group, the International Monetary Fund, and representatives of security-focused think tanks. Discussions focused on regional developments, preventive diplomacy and UNRCCA's priorities, including preventing violent extremism conducive to terrorism, climate change and transboundary water management, and the Women, Peace and Security and Youth, Peace and Security agendas.

This week, Jean Arnault, Officer-in-Charge of the Office of the United Nations Special Coordinator for Lebanon (UNSCOL) [and Personal Envoy of the Secretary-General on the Middle East conflict and its consequences], visited Tripoli and Akkar in northern Lebanon, Sidon in the south, and Zahleh and Baalbek in the east to engage with local authorities, communities and the Lebanese Armed Forces (LAF) on ways to strengthen security, stability and social cohesion. During the visit, he toured UN-supported initiatives promoting livelihoods and resilience, met with displaced Lebanese and Syrian refugees, and reaffirmed the United Nations' commitment to supporting communities across the country. Concluding his tour with a visit to an LAF border regiment, he pledged to continue mobilizing international support to help strengthen State authority.

On 25 July, the UN Verification Mission in Colombia (UNVMC) accompanied We Effect Latin America on a visit to productive initiatives led by the peace signatories' cooperative COOMPAZCOL in Conejo, La Guajira. The visit highlighted how tailoring, agricultural production and community enterprises are supporting sustainable reintegration and local development, with women playing a leading role in strengthening the cooperative's resilience and long-term sustainability.

Between 26 and 27 July, SRSG and Head of the UNVMC Miroslav Jenča visited the department of Chocó , where he met with peace signatories, ethnic representatives, State institutions and civil society to discuss progress and persistent challenges in implementing the Final Peace Agreement. In Quibdó, he highlighted the resilience of a fish farming project led by peace signatories as an example of the potential of reintegration. The SRSG also met with representatives of the Colombian Army, the Ombudsperson's Office, the Catholic Church and the Inter-Ethnic Solidarity Forum of Chocó (FISCH) to discuss the humanitarian situation and security guarantees for communities. He emphasized that "even in complex contexts, progress is possible through perseverance, collective effort and a determined commitment to implementing the Final Peace Agreement."

From 27 to 29 July, senior representatives from the United Nations and the League of Arab States (LAS) met in Geneva for the General Cooperation Meeting between the two organizations and their specialized bodies. Co-chaired by Assistant Secretary-General (ASG) Khaled Khiari and LAS Assistant Secretary-General Khaled Manzlawiy, the meeting brought together around 40 UN and LAS entities to strengthen collaboration on shared priorities. In his opening remarks, ASG Khiari underscored that cooperation and joint action are "force multipliers" that enable both organizations to deliver greater impact in advancing peace, security and sustainable development.

From 26 to 28 July, the United Nations Transitional Mission in Somalia (UNTMIS) supported a three-day Digital Newsroom Transformation training in Garowe, organized by the Puntland Ministry of Information. The training brought together 25 journalists to strengthen skills in mobile journalism, digital storytelling and multimedia production, while reinforcing ethical reporting, content verification and audience engagement across digital platforms.

Concluding a week of first contacts with Chadian authorities during a mission in N'Djamena, Special Representative of the Secretary-General (SRSG) and Head of the United Nations Office for Central Africa (UNOCA) Mohamed El-Amine Souef was received in audience by President Mahamat Idriss Déby Itno. During the mission, SRSG Souef met with the Prime Minister, the Minister of Foreign Affairs, the Ombudsman of the Republic, the First Vice-President of the National Assembly, representatives of the diplomatic community, the Resident Coordinator and the United Nations country team.

On 1 August, in Agua Bonita, Caquetá, the United Nations Verification Mission in Colombia (UNVMC) accompanied the closing of Sowing the Amazon: Harvesting Peace and Reconciliation, a community initiative that strengthened local capacities on gender equality and countering stigmatization through women’s associations and educational institutions. Participants reaffirmed the importance of community engagement in advancing reconciliation, peaceful coexistence and sustainable peace through art, dialogue and shared experiences.

Jean Arnault, Officer-in-Charge of the Office of the United Nations Special Coordinator for Lebanon (UNSCOL) [and Personal Envoy of the Secretary-General on the Middle East conflict and its consequences], visited southern Lebanon, where he called for enhanced international support to the Lebanese Armed Forces to help extend State authority and stability. He also met with senior Lebanese officials to discuss the implementation of Security Council resolution 1701 (2006), international support, and cooperation between Lebanon and the United Nations. Earlier in the week, he joined members of the diplomatic community in commemorating the sixth anniversary of the Beirut Port explosion, reaffirming support for truth, justice, accountability and judicial independence.

This week, the United Nations Transitional Mission in Somalia (UNTMIS) supported a four-day BRIDGE Electoral Observation workshop in Mogadishu for civil society representatives from Somalia's Federal Member States and Banaadir. The training strengthened participants' skills in election observation, international standards and reporting, contributing to preparations for upcoming elections
The Security Council is expected to hold a briefing on the Middle East (Yemen) on 13 August.

Briefing the Security Council on Ukraine on 24 August, marking four and a half years since the start of the Russian Federation’s full-scale invasion, USG DiCarlo warned a mounting civilian toll and continued escalation, including attacks affecting civilian and maritime infrastructure. She stressed that the need to end the war “could not be more urgent”, calling for every available diplomatic effort to be mobilized to de-escalate the conflict.

On 27 August, Deputy Special Envoy of the Secretary-General (DSESG) for Syria Claudio Cordone spoke at the Security Council from Damascus on developments in Syria’s political transition. Building on the Secretary-General’s recent visit, DSESG Cordone stressed that the transition’s success will ultimately depend on whether all Syrians are represented and able to participate meaningfully in shaping the country’s future. He also underscored the importance of accountability, transitional justice and the meaningful participation of women and civil society.

On 21 August, the Special Representative of the Secretary-General (SRSG) and Head of the United Nations Regional Centre for Preventive Diplomacy for Central Asia (UNRCCA) , Kaha Imnadze, met with Tajikistan’s Foreign Minister Sirojiddin Muhriddin in Ashgabat to discuss regional developments and cooperation between Tajikistan and UNRCCA. Their discussions focused on priorities including implementation of the General Assembly resolution on the International Decade for Strengthening of Peace for Future Generations (2027–2036).

During a visit to Badakhshan province this week, Acting Head of the United Nations Assistance Mission in Afghanistan (UNAMA) and Deputy Special Representative of the Secretary-General (DSRSG) Georgette Gagnon met with local authorities, women entrepreneurs, community leaders and other stakeholders to discuss challenges facing communities, particularly women, and efforts to address the impact of narcotics. In Faizabad and Khash district, she visited UN-supported initiatives, including a drug rehabilitation centre, a women’s safe space and a women-led dairy processing enterprise providing an alternative to poppy cultivation. DSRSG Gagnon called for greater investment in alternative development opportunities and sustainable livelihoods while reaffirming the UN’s support for communities across Afghanistan.

On 25 August, SRSG and Head of the United Nations Regional Office for Central Africa (UNOCA) Mohamed El-Amine Souef met with President Obiang Nguema Mbasogo in Malabo during his first mission to Equatorial Guinea as Head of UNOCA. Discussions focused on peace and social cohesion in Central Africa, conflict prevention, and the role of women and youth. The SRSG reaffirmed UNOCA’s commitment to supporting regional cooperation and the efforts of the Economic Community of Central African States (ECCAS). During his visit, Souef also met with Vice-President Teodoro Nguema Obiang Mangue.

On 28 August, SRSG and Head of the United Nations Support Mission in Libya (UNSMIL) Hanna Tetteh had discussions in Benghazi with LNA Deputy General Commander Lt. Gen. Saddam Haftar political, economic and security developments in Libya. The SRSG welcomed the General Command delegation’s constructive engagement in the Smaller Convening, which resulted in agreement on the first two milestones of the UN-facilitated roadmap: the High National Elections Commission and the legal framework for presidential and parliamentary elections. She called on the eastern authorities to build on this momentum to help break the political deadlock and advance legitimate, accountable and unified institutions.

On 26 August, Greek Cypriot leader Nikos Christodoulides and Turkish Cypriot leader Tufan Erhürman met in Nicosia under United Nations auspices and agreed to intensify their engagement, including by meeting once a week and more frequently as circumstances may require. The meeting followed the Secretary-General’s July visit to Cyprus, when he announced his intention to convene another 5+1 meeting after adequate preparations on confidence-building, methodology and substance. The UN Good Offices Mission in Cyprus continues to support the Secretary-General and his Personal Envoy in facilitating dialogue, building trust and advancing the peace process.

On 27 August in Morales, Cauca, peace signatories joined local communities for a day of art and culture, creating a mural with messages of peace and reconciliation and helping strengthen dialogue, trust and peaceful coexistence.

On 28 August, Special Representative of the Secretary-General (SRSG) and Head of the United Nations Integrated Office in Haiti (BINUH) Carlos Ruiz Massieu briefed the Security Council meeting following a deadly gang attack in Kenscoff that killed at least 47 people, including five children. Condemning the attack, he called for the immediate release of those abducted and stressed the urgent need to strengthen international security support for Haiti. He emphasized that security efforts must go hand in hand with restoring State authority, basic services and livelihoods, advancing the political process and ensuring accountability. “Haiti urgently needs existing commitments to translate into concrete results,” he said.

On 4 September, the Personal Envoy of the Secretary-General for Sudan, Pekka Haavisto, travelled to Khartoum to engage key stakeholders on measures to de-escalate violence and strengthen the protection of civilians. Next week, he will be joined by partners from the Quintet (the African Union, European Union, IGAD and League of Arab States) for a joint visit focused on the political landscape and efforts to advance intra-Sudanese dialogue.

This week, Special Envoy of the Secretary-General (SESG) for the Great Lakes Region Huang Xia visited Burundi, Rwanda and Uganda, together with SRSG and Head of MONUSCO James Swan, as part of UN efforts to support durable peace in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo and coordinate regional peace initiatives. They reiterated UN support for African Union-led mediation efforts and called on all parties to comply with Security Council resolution 2773 and fulfil their commitments under the ongoing Doha and Washington processes.

This week, Personal Envoy of the Secretary-General for Sudan Pekka Haavisto joined the Quintet (the African Union, IGAD, League of Arab States, European Union and United Nations) for a good-offices mission to Khartoum. The Quintet met with senior officials and political and civilian actors, listening to Sudanese perspectives and seeking to connect international efforts with initiatives emerging inside the country. At the conclusion of the mission, the Quintet reiterated its commitment to a credible, inclusive, Sudanese-led and Sudanese-owned political process towards a democratic, civilian-led government reflecting the aspirations of the Sudanese people.

On 9 September, the UN Good Offices Mission in Cyprus hosted Greek Cypriot leader Nikos Christodoulides and Turkish Cypriot leader Tufan Erhürman. The meeting came ahead of their expected travel to New York, where they are due to meet separately with UN officials on the sidelines of the General Assembly high-level week. The Good Offices Mission continues to support the Secretary-General and his Personal Envoy in sustaining dialogue and advancing the peace process.

On 9 September, the United Nations Regional Centre for Preventive Diplomacy for Central Asia (UNRCCA) brought together young professionals from Central Asia and Afghanistan participating in its Preventive Diplomacy Academy for a session on humanitarian action and international humanitarian law, led by experts from the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC). Participants explored the foundations and application of international humanitarian law and discussed contemporary challenges, including urban warfare and cyber operations, as part of the Academy’s efforts to strengthen capacities in conflict prevention and preventive diplomacy.

On 9 September, more than 40 missions joined the DPPA Donor Group meeting, hosted by the Permanent Mission of Norway to the United Nations. As the Department develops its next Strategic Plan and Multi-Year Appeal (MYA) for 2027–2030, the meeting provided an opportunity to hear partners’ perspectives on the priorities and challenges that will shape DPPA’s work in the years ahead. Reaffirming their support for DPPA, partners also underscored the MYA's role in providing flexible funding to support DPPA’s work and deliver on its mandate.

On 15 September, Assistant Secretary-General (ASG) for the Middle East, Europe, the Americas, Asia and the Pacific, Khaled Khiari, briefed the Security Council on the intensifying conflict in Yemen and growing volatility around the Bab al-Mandab Strait. With fighting expanding across multiple frontlines and at least 125,000 people displaced since the start of the month, ASG Khiari called on all parties to protect civilians, respect international humanitarian law and prevent further escalation. He also stressed the need to safeguard freedom of navigation in the Red Sea and urged the parties to prioritize dialogue and engage constructively with UN-led efforts towards a negotiated political solution.

This week, Officer-in-Charge of the Office of the United Nations Special Coordinator for Lebanon (UNSCOL) [and Personal Envoy of the Secretary-General on the Middle East conflict and its consequences] Jean Arnault participated in an Aqaba Process meeting in Paris, where international and regional partners discussed coordinating support for the Lebanese Armed Forces (LAF), including its security and capability needs. He underscored the importance of sustained international support for the LAF and other State institutions as Lebanon works to strengthen State authority and security across the country.

On 15 September, Personal Envoy of the Secretary-General for Sudan Pekka Haavisto concluded a two-day visit to Egypt, following his recent mission to Sudan. In Cairo, he met with senior Egyptian officials and the Secretary-General of the League of Arab States to discuss regional efforts to advance peace and strengthen coordination through the Quad and Quintet. Haavisto also met with members of the Sudanese diaspora, underscoring the importance of ensuring that Sudan’s diverse voices contribute meaningfully to shaping the country’s future.

This week, SRSG and Head of the United Nations Regional Office for Central Africa (UNOCA) Mohamed El-Amine Souef met with President Brice Clotaire Oligui Nguema in Gabon. He also undertook his first official visit to the Central African Republic and met President Faustin-Archange Touadéra. Discussions focused on national and regional peace and security, including political dialogue, peacebuilding and social cohesion. In Bangui, Souef also highlighted the increasingly transboundary nature of challenges facing the region, including the conflict in Sudan, population movements, illicit arms trafficking, transhumance and climate change, and stressed the importance of early warning, preventive diplomacy and regional cooperation.

On 16 September, the Preventive Diplomacy Academy of the United Nations Regional Centre for Preventive Diplomacy for Central Asia (UNRCCA) brought together young professionals from Central Asia and Afghanistan for an online session on youth inclusion in peace processes. Participants explored practical approaches to engaging young people in peacemaking, dialogue and conflict prevention, including through an interactive exercise. The session was part of the Academy’s broader efforts to strengthen the knowledge, skills and regional networks of young peacebuilders.

On 15 September, SRSG and Head of the United Nations Office for West Africa and the Sahel (UNOWAS) Leonardo Santos Simão began a visit to Mauritania as part of his ongoing efforts to promote peace, stability and dialogue in the subregion. In Nouakchott, he was expected to meet with President Mohamed Ould Cheikh El Ghazouani, government officials and representatives of the ruling party and opposition, among others. The SRSG also visited the Hodh El Chargui region, including the Mbera refugee camp, to engage with local authorities, refugees and humanitarian and development partners.

On 14 September, UNOWAS and the UNESCO Regional Office for West Africa convened UN Resident Coordinators from across the region to discuss the implementation of the Regional Action Plan on Information Integrity . SRSG Simão underscored the importance of information integrity for peace, social cohesion and good governance, as well as the role of UN Country Teams in integrating it into conflict prevention, peacebuilding and development efforts. Participants also discussed concrete measures to translate the regional plan into initiatives adapted to national contexts.

On 18 September, UN colleagues, family and friends gathered in New York to honor the memory and legacy of Nicholas “Fink” Haysom, who served the United Nations in Iraq, Afghanistan, Sudan, Somalia and South Sudan. In her remarks , USG Rosemary DiCarlo remembered Haysom as “a peacemaker and a mediator of rare intuition” whose ability to listen, build trust and bring people together shaped his decades of work for peace. She paid tribute to his unwavering dedication to humanity, his belief in dialogue and his lifelong commitment to peace and extended her condolences to his family.

The tributes reflected a legacy rooted in Haysom’s conviction that even in the most difficult circumstances, common ground could be found through dialogue, patience and an unwavering commitment to peace.

“Peacebuilding and development both begin and hold when people’s rights are protected and they can trust the institutions that serve them. With this important support from the Government of the Netherlands, we will advance inclusive governance, strengthen institutions and contribute to lasting peace,” said Alexander De Croo, UNDP Administrator . “This agreement also gives us something essential: time. Justice systems and public trust cannot be rebuilt within a twelve-month project. Predictable, multi-year funding allows us to stay the course, build lasting partnerships and prevent crises from deepening.”

DPPA was actively engaged throughout the UN General Assembly High-Level Week. Under-Secretary-General (USG) Rosemary DiCarlo met several delegations, in addition to her participation in several of the Secretary-General bilateral meetings. She addressed the Security Council high-level meeting on Ukraine and participated in high-level discussions on Sudan, with the Group of friends of mediation, as well as on cooperation between the Security Council and the League of Arab States. Nine Special Representatives, Special Envoys and Personal Envoys of the Secretary-General were also in New York this week to engage with Member States and partners on peace and security priorities spanning Haiti, the Middle East, Myanmar, Cyprus, West Africa and the Sahel, the Great Lakes region, Sudan, Syria and more. Together, these engagements advanced the Secretary-General’s conflict-resolution efforts, preven

On 24 September, USG DiCarlo addressed a high-level dialogue on cooperation between the Security Council and the League of Arab States (LAS), stressing that closer cooperation can help advance diplomacy, reduce tensions and support political solutions across the region, including on Yemen, the Occupied Palestinian Territory, Lebanon, Syria, Sudan, Libya and Somalia. Against the backdrop of escalating regional tensions, she emphasized that “diplomacy must be given every opportunity to succeed,” describing the UN-LAS partnership as a “force multiplier” for advancing shared peace and security objectives.

Officer-in-Charge of the Office of the United Nations Special Coordinator for Lebanon (UNSCOL) [and Personal Envoy of the Secretary-General on the Middle East conflict and its consequences] Jean Arnault visited the Adyan Foundation in Beirut, where he met with its President, Nayla Tabbara, and representatives of different religious communities. Discussions focused on responsible citizenship, religious dialogue and social cohesion. The OiC underscored the importance of building national consensus amid Lebanon’s diversity, including as a means of strengthening international support for the country.

On 23 September, Acting Special Coordinator for the Middle East Peace Process Ramiz Alakbarov addressed a high-level roundtable on Gaza’s early recovery, stressing that recovery and political progress must advance together. Following a three-day visit to Gaza, he called for improved humanitarian and operational access, the rapid restoration of essential services and stronger coordination to translate financing into tangible improvements for Palestinians. The Acting Special Coordinator emphasized that recovery should be Palestinian-led and support the reunification of Gaza and the West Bank under a single, legitimate Palestinian government and a renewed political process towards a two-State solution.

On 25 September, DPPA signed a new multi-year funding agreement covering 2027–2029 with Iceland, representing a total commitment of ISK 120 million (approximately US$1 million) over three years. The agreement provides annual flexible funding to DPPA’s Multi-Year Appeal (MYA) as well as dedicated support for the Department’s work in the Middle East. Iceland and DPPA also held a strategic dialogue on developments in the Middle East, Sudan and Ukraine. The continued partnership underscores the importance of predictable and flexible funding in enabling DPPA to respond to emerging priorities and sustain its conflict prevention and peacemaking efforts.

On 23 September, the Preventive Diplomacy Academy of the United Nations Regional Centre for Preventive Diplomacy for Central Asia (UNRCCA) brought together its 2026 cohort for an online session with CMI – Martti Ahtisaari Peace Foundation on mediation and the use of digital tools in peace efforts. Participants explored how technology can support communication and engagement in mediation and dialogue, linking practical experience with the Academy’s broader work to strengthen skills in conflict prevention and preventive diplomacy.

On 20 September, members of the Smaller Convening met in Tunis under the chairmanship of SRSG and Head of the United Nations Support Mission in Libya (UNSMIL) Hanna Tetteh to follow up on implementation of the agreement signed on 30 August. Participants reaffirmed their commitment to advancing the agreement towards national elections and agreed to continue engaging Libyan stakeholders to build broader support. The meeting was the first since the agreement to reconstitute the High National Elections Commission and amend electoral laws.

On 21 September, the Steering Committee of the Consultative Body for Civil Society Engagement in the Cyprus peace process held its first meeting , following the appointment of its 10 members by the two Cypriot leaders. Facilitated by the UN Good Offices Mission in Cyprus , the Committee began discussions on working methods and plans for the Consultative Body, which is intended to strengthen meaningful civil society participation in the peace process. The initiative was among the trust-building measures agreed by the leaders at the informal 5+1 meeting convened by the Secretary-General in July 2025.

From 21 to 23 September, representatives from across the Horn of Africa gathered in Nairobi for a three-day workshop aimed at strengthening regional capacity to monitor, analyse and address hate speech and disinformation.

The workshop was led jointly by the Office of the Special Envoy of the Secretary-General for the Horn of Africa, the DPPA Innovation Cell and the Department of Peace Operations Information Integrity Unit, in partnership with the African Union (AU) and the Intergovernmental Authority on Development (IGAD).

Bringing together participants from the AU, IGAD, civil society organizations and United Nations entities working across the region, the workshop provided a platform to exchange experiences and approaches to navigating an increasingly complex information environment.

The workshop underscored the importance of cooperation among regional organizations, the United Nations and civil society in strengthening information integrity and supporting efforts to prevent tensions and advance peace and stability across the Horn of Africa.

Earlier in the week, on 30 September, Mr. Grundberg concluded a visit to Cairo , where he met with Egypt’s Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty and League of Arab States Secretary-General Nabil Fahmy. Discussions focused on the recent escalation in Yemen and its regional repercussions, including in the Red Sea, as well as UN efforts to achieve a sustainable end to the conflict. Grundberg expressed appreciation for the continued support of Egypt and the League of Arab States for UN mediation efforts.

On 2 October, Officer-in-Charge of the Office of the United Nations Special Coordinator for Lebanon (UNSCOL) [and Personal Envoy of the Secretary-General on the Middle East conflict and its consequences] Jean Arnault visited Nabatieh in southern Lebanon, where he met with local communities affected by widespread destruction. Residents expressed their desire to live in peace and security under a State responsive to their needs. Arnault commended the resilience and determination of the people of Nabatieh to rebuild their lives, homes and city despite the challenges they continue to face.

On 29 September, the United Nations Support Mission in Libya (UNSMIL) invited civil society organizations and community leaders across Libya to organize public consultations on implementing the recommendations of the Structured Dialogue . Developed through six months of deliberations involving some 120 Libyans, the recommendations address governance, security, the economy, national reconciliation and human rights. The Mission also launched a toolkit to facilitate discussions and gather community feedback on implementation priorities. DSRSG Stephanie Koury stressed the importance of ensuring that Libyans’ voices guide the next steps in translating the recommendations into concrete action.

On 28 September, UNSMIL reported that implementing partners, with support from its Mine Action Programme, had cleared 14,066 items of explosive ordnance from Al-Sweihli Farm in Misratah between January and September 2026. During a field visit , the UNSMIL Mine Action team met with local authorities and partners to review clearance efforts and discuss remaining threats to civilian safety. The Mission also highlighted the importance of strengthening national capacities in weapons and ammunition management, raising awareness of explosive hazards and preventing unplanned explosions near populated areas.

On 30 September, in Jacmel, southeastern Haiti, around 60 young women and men participated in a dialogue on the electoral process, organized through a partnership between the United Nations Integrated Office in Haiti (BINUH) , Haitian institutions and civil society organizations. Discussions focused on strengthening voter registration, addressing logistical and security challenges to holding elections, and encouraging young people’s participation in public life. The initiative forms part of ongoing efforts to engage first-time voters and promote informed civic participation in Haiti.

On 26 September, the UN–AU Joint Task Force on Peace and Security held its 27th consultative meeting in New York, bringing together senior officials, including USG Rosemary DiCarlo, to review their partnership and discuss developments across Africa. Discussions focused on the eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, the Horn of Africa, Somalia, South Sudan and Sudan, with an emphasis on de-escalation, inclusive political processes and coordinated mediation efforts. The meeting also highlighted progress in implementing Security Council resolution 2719 (2023) on financing AU-led peace support operations and reaffirmed the importance of strengthening cooperation on conflict prevention, peacebuilding and operational support.

On 30 September, Special Representative of the Secretary-General (SRSG) and Head of the United Nations Regional Centre for Preventive Diplomacy for Central Asia (UNRCCA) Kaha Imnadze visited Tajikistan’s Sughd region to assess progress in implementing the bilateral border agreement between Tajikistan and Kyrgyzstan and its impact on local communities. During visits to border areas, he learned about strengthened cross-border communication, the gradual restoration of trade and ongoing border demarcation efforts. Imnadze also visited a UNEP-supported initiative addressing climate and environmental risks. Welcoming the progress achieved, he underscored the importance of sustained dialogue, confidence-building and practical cooperation in promoting regional stability and good-neighbourly relations.

On 30 September, UNRCCA’s Preventive Diplomacy Academy convened its first Peace Circle , bringing together young participants from Central Asia and Afghanistan to exchange perspectives on shared challenges and opportunities for cooperation. Discussions focused on gender equality, climate, peace and security, and economic opportunities, highlighting the connections between these issues and their impact on young people’s lives. The initiative provided a platform for youth to explore practical solutions and contribute their perspectives to peacebuilding efforts in the region.

During a visit to Côte d’Ivoire this week, SRSG and Head of the United Nations Office for West Africa and the Sahel (UNOWAS) Leonardo Santos Simão engaged Ivorian authorities on regional peace, security and stability. On 28 September, he participated in a high-level regional event on women, youth, peace, security and economic resilience. The event focused on strengthening economic opportunities for women and young people as a means of advancing conflict prevention, peacebuilding and resilience across West Africa and the Sahel. At the opening ceremony, SRSG and Head of UNOWAS Leonardo Santos Simão stressed that sustainable peace requires inclusion, economic opportunities and the full participation of women and youth, describing investment in their empowerment as a strategic investment in regional peace and stability.

The following day, Mr. Simão met with Interior and Security Minister Vagondo Diomandé and signed a Memorandum of Understanding with the Conseil de l’Entente to strengthen cooperation on peace and security in West Africa and the Sahel. His visit also includes engagements on cross-border security and the protection of displaced populations.

From 21 to 25 September, UNOWAS engaged regional partners in Accra and Abidjan to strengthen cooperation on climate, peace and security. At an ECOWAS Parliament seminar in Accra, UNOWAS highlighted the links between climate shocks, displacement and insecurity, and the role of parliamentarians in translating policy commitments into action. At the ECOWAS Regional Water Forum in Abidjan, discussions focused on transboundary water cooperation and shared natural resource management as tools for dialogue, trust-building and conflict prevention. UNOWAS also engaged Ivorian authorities on integrating peace and security considerations into national climate strategies.

On 1 October, the UN Verification Mission in Colombia joined victims, Peace Agreement signatories, women’s groups and young people in Baraya, Huila, for the inauguration of the House for Integration, Memory and Peace, an initiative of Colombia’s Agency for Reincorporation and Normalization (ARN). The new community space aims to foster dialogue, coexistence and local integration, bringing together diverse voices to strengthen social ties and advance reconciliation and peacebuilding.

On 26 September, the UN Verification Mission in Colombia brought its Pathways Colombia virtual reality experience to Reading Under the Trees, an outdoor literary festival in Bogotá. Through immersive storytelling, participants explored stories of peace and Peace Agreement implementation, reflecting on the experiences of those involved in the peace process. The initiative encouraged dialogue and understanding, with participants sharing reflections and messages of support for peace and Peace Agreement signatories.

On Tuesday, the Security Council will hold a meeting on cooperation between the United Nations and regional and subregional organizations, focusing on the African Union. On Friday, the Council will meet to discuss the situation in Yemen.

This afternoon, Khaled Khiari, the Assistant Secretary-General for the Middle East, Europe, the Americas, Asia and the Pacific, briefed the Security Council on the situation in Ukraine. He told Council members that since our last briefing on 23 September, the attacks by the Russian Federation on Ukraine have reached a new horrifying level. He highlighted the surge in civilian casualties caused by intensified Russian attacks, including strikes on residential areas, transport networks, energy infrastructure and educational institutions. He also expressed concern over civilian casualties resulting from Ukrainian attacks inside the Russian Federation. Jean Arnault, the Officer-in-Charge of the Office of the United Nations Special Coordinator for Lebanon (UNSCOL) [and Personal Envoy of the Secretary-General on the Middle East conflict and its consequences] met with President Joseph Aoun today. They discussed recent developments in Lebanon and the region and the continued engagement of the United Nations in Lebanon.

On 9 October, Special Envoy of the Secretary-General (SESG) for Yemen Hans Grundberg warned the Security Council that Yemen had returned to full-scale war , with fighting intensifying across multiple frontlines and the humanitarian situation deteriorating, particularly in Taiz. Urging all parties to respect international humanitarian law, he stressed that military gains cannot replace negotiations and called for a credible, Yemeni-owned political process. He also renewed his call for the unconditional release of 72 UN personnel detained by the Houthis. Earlier, on 6 October, Mr. Grundberg concluded a visit to Washington, D.C. , where he discussed developments in Yemen and regional security with senior US officials, underscoring the importance of sustained international support for a political solution.

Briefing the Security Council on 9 October, Assistant Secretary-General (ASG) for the Middle East, Europe, the Americas, Asia and the Pacific Khaled Khiari warned the Security Council of a sharp escalation in attacks on Ukraine, with more than 100 civilians killed and at least 429 injured in the past week, according to OHCHR. He condemned attacks against civilians and civilian infrastructure, highlighting growing damage to energy facilities ahead of winter and the risks posed by attacks on commercial shipping in the Black Sea. Mr. Khiari also expressed concern over civilian casualties in the Russian Federation and the dire humanitarian situation in Russian-occupied areas of Ukraine. On 6 October, Under-Secretary-General (USG) for Political and Peacebuilding Affairs Rosemary DiCarlo concluded a visit to Afghanistan , where she met with the de facto authorities, civil society representatives, women leaders and Afghan female UN personnel. She reaffirmed the UN’s commitment to advancing the Doha process, noting progress in working groups on counter-narcotics and the private sector while calling for further practical results. USG DiCarlo also raised concerns about restrictions on women and girls, including access to education and those affecting Afghan female UN personnel. She underscored the UN’s continued support for the Afghan people amid socioeconomic, climate-related and humanitarian challenges.

From 4 to 6 October, Officer-in-Charge of the Office of the United Nations Special Coordinator for Lebanon (UNSCOL) [and Personal Envoy of the Secretary-General on the Middle East conflict and its consequences] Jean Arnault visited Tehran, where he met with Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi to discuss regional developments and prospects for international cooperation in support of peace and stability. On 9 October, Mr. Arnault met with Lebanese President Joseph Aoun to exchange views on developments in Lebanon and the wider region, as well as the UN’s continued engagement in the country.

On 4 October, SRSG and Head of the United Nations Office for West Africa and the Sahel (UNOWAS) Leonardo Santos Simão concluded a week-long good offices mission to Côte d’Ivoire , where he engaged government officials and political parties on national dialogue, electoral reform and regional peace and security. During the visit, He met with Ivorian authorities, as well as opposition parties and the ruling party to discuss peace and security, electoral reform and national political dialogue. On 29 September, he signed a Memorandum of Understanding with the Conseil de l’Entente to strengthen cooperation on preventive diplomacy, early warning, mediation and peacebuilding. He also visited the Korhogo region to learn about efforts to support refugees.

On 8 October, Deputy SRSG of UNOWAS Barrie Freeman addressed the opening of the NGO Forum in Dakar, ahead of the 89th Ordinary Session of the African Commission on Human and Peoples’ Rights. She highlighted the links between human rights, climate resilience and conflict prevention, stressing that equitable water management can help reduce tensions between communities. Freeman also underscored the vital role of civil society in protecting human rights and strengthening accountability, while expressing concern over growing restrictions on civic space. "NGOs have the right to operate in a safe and enabling environment," she said, reaffirming UNOWAS' commitment to stand alongside civil society in defending civic space.

From 6 to 8 October, the United Nations Regional Centre for Preventive Diplomacy for Central Asia (UNRCCA) participated in a regional conference on countering terrorism and extremism in Minsk, Belarus, bringing together representatives of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO), the Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS), UN entities and other international partners. Discussions focused on regional counter-terrorism cooperation, terrorist financing and the role of emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence. UNRCCA highlighted its work to advance implementation of the UN Global Counter-Terrorism Strategy in Central Asia through the Joint Plan of Action, including a multi-year project with the UN Office of Counter-Terrorism and regional partners.

On 3 October, the United Nations Verification Mission in Colombia (UNVMC) joined UNDP Colombia and the Municipal Peace Council for a community event in La Capilla, Corinto, Cauca, as part of Colombia’s Month for Peace. Bringing together different generations, the event promoted dialogue, peaceful coexistence and community participation in peacebuilding. The Mission engaged children through recreational and environmental activities and introduced its Pathways Colombia virtual reality experience, highlighting stories of peacebuilding. Community members also met with representatives of the Cauca Governor’s Office to discuss conflict resolution mechanisms and gender-related issues.

On 3 October, students from several schools gathered in San Martín, Meta, for the fourth Inter-School Human Rights Meeting, organized by the Municipal Peace Council with support from the United Nations Verification Mission in Colombia (UNVMC) . Led by the Mayor’s Office and the Municipal Ombudsperson’s Office, the event focused on the rights of children affected by armed conflict, women’s rights and gender equality. Students shared their perspectives and discussed how young people can contribute to peacebuilding, respect for human rights and more inclusive communities.

From 24 September to 2 October, a UN electoral needs assessment mission led by DPPA’s Electoral Assistance Division visited Timor-Leste at the Government’s request. Ahead of presidential elections expected in March 2027, potential municipal elections later that year and parliamentary elections in 2028, the mission met with the Prime Minister, national stakeholders and international partners to assess priorities and discuss possible UN support. Building on the country’s electoral achievements, any UN support would aim to further strengthen national capacity and promote trust and inclusive participation among voters, political parties and the broader public.

On 6 October, the Peacebuilding and Peace Support Office (PBPSO) convened a workshop in New York to review preliminary findings and recommendations from the independent evaluation of the Peacebuilding Fund (PBF) Strategy 2020–2026. Bringing together government and civil society representatives from programme countries and evaluation stakeholders, discussions highlighted the Fund’s role in supporting nationally owned peacebuilding and prevention efforts. On 7 October, participants also discussed priorities for the next PBF strategy, emphasizing nationally led prevention, whole-of-society approaches, innovative financing partnerships and evidence-based learning. The meetings formed part of a broader consultation process to shape the Fund’s future direction amid growing peacebuilding needs and constrained resources.

Next week, the Security Council will hold briefings on Colombia and Syria on Monday, 12 October, followed by the Great Lakes region on 13 October and the United Nations Support Mission in Libya (UNSMIL) on 14 October. On 15 October, the Council will convene an open debate on the situation in the Middle East. The week will conclude on 16 October with discussions on Sudan, including resolution 2715 (2023), and a briefing by the Security Council Committee established pursuant to resolution 1591 (2005) concerning the Sudan.

Women’s meaningful participation in shaping peace efforts in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) and the wider Great Lakes region took centre stage at a high-level event jointly convened by the United Nations, African Union and European Union on 21 September, on the margins of the UN General Assembly in New York.

The head of the United Nations Office for Central Africa (UNOCA), Mohamed El Amine Souef, arrived in Yaoundé, Cameroon, today, for a working visit. During his visit, he will meet with Cameroonian national authorities to strengthen collaboration between Cameroon and UNOCA.
Elizabeth Spehar , the Assistant Secretary-General for Peacebuilding and Peace Support was at the Geneva Peace Forum today.

She took part in a discussion with Annyssa Bellal, the Executive Director of the Geneva Peace Forum, on what champions of peacebuilding can do to support the United Nations' work and communicate the impact of peacebuilders around the world.
